observation.visible_scene: A near-black room lit only by a small flame (a candle or fire in a low container) positioned center-frame on top of a dark, round silhouette (a stool or table edge) in the foreground. A faint background wall with a thin horizontal line (beam or shelf) sits near the top, and a glass-like surface produces a mirrored reflection of the flame below the source. The view is handheld and dim, with the flame as the dominant light source.
visible_changes: The flame's height and brightness oscillate continuously: it flares into a tall, bright tongue (e.g. frames 1, 8, 15-16, 23-24, 27-28, 31) and then collapses to a tiny glow or is hidden behind the foreground silhouette (e.g. frames 2-6, 10-11, 13, 19-22, 25, 32-33), with no onset or termination visible.

A separate bright patch below the flame (its reflection in the glass/container) appears and fades in step with the flame's height, clearly resolved as a candle-in-glass with reflection in frames 12 and 17, and as a mirrored flame in frame 1.

The dark round foreground silhouette and the background horizontal line drift slightly in position and visible extent from frame to frame, consistent with small handheld camera jitter rather than movement of the stand itself.
The flame's apparent vertical position relative to the silhouette's top edge changes, reflecting the combination of the flame growing/shrinking and the minor camera shake.
The overall scene brightness and the size of the illuminated halo on the wall rise and fall with the flame, but no new objects enter or leave the frame.
outside_clip_unknowns: What fuel or object produces the flame and whether anything is being added or adjusted to it is not shown.
The identity and purpose of the round foreground stand and the glass surface are not established.
Whether the flame's flickering is natural or driven by an unseen draft or operator is unknown.
The start and end of the burning process lie outside this cropped segment.
uncertain_details: Distinguishing pure camera shake from actual movement of the flame/stand is difficult in the dark; the silhouette's small shifts may be partly jitter.
The reflection is sometimes mistaken for a second flame; it tracks the source's height, supporting a reflection interpretation, but the exact geometry of the glass is unclear.
The frame-12/17 fully-visible candle and the otherwise silhouette-obscured flame are treated as the same source at different flicker states, not as two different objects.
